source.citation: Chen N, Wen L, Lau H, Surapaneni S, Kumar G. Pharmacokinetics, metabolism and excretion of [14C]-lenalidomide following oral administration in healthy male subjects. Cancer Chemother Pharmacol 2012;69:789-797.
source.storage: Kept on the platform owner's computer; not committed (the same file as lenalidomide_blood_plasma_chen_2012_v1.json).
source.extraction: AI-assisted from the PDF text layer; each quote checked against the extracted text. Independent review pending.

urine_radioactivity_pct_dose.quote: A total of 90.3 ± 3.0% (range: 87.0–94.6%) of dose was recovered in urine, which indicates the oral absorption of lenalidomide was high.

total_recovery_pct_dose.quote: The total recovery of the radioactivity over 10 days averaged 94.3 ± 2.9% (range: 90.5–97.2%) of the administered dose

feces_radioactivity_pct_dose.quote: Urinary excretion was the primary route of elimination (90% of radioactive dose), with minor amounts excreted in feces (4%).

parent_share_of_urine_radioactivity.quote: Lenalidomide was the primary radioactive component in plasma (92% of the [14C]-area under the concentration–time curve) and urine (>90% of the radioactivity in urine).
parent_share_of_urine_radioactivity.location: Abstract (PDF page 1); the text layer renders ">" as "[".

unchanged_in_urine_pct_dose_cited.quote: Excretion of the unchanged parent in urine is the predominant clearance mechanism of lenalidomide, accounting for approximately 84% of the dose [15].

authors_conclusion.quote: lenalidomide is highly absorbed and bioavailable, metabolized minimally, and eliminated predominantly via urinary excretion in the unchanged form in humans.

use_on_platform.bioavailability_bounds: Radioactivity recovered in urine was absorbed, so the fraction absorbed is at least about 0.90 (mean 90.3%, individual range 87.0-94.6%). Unchanged drug in urine (about 0.84-0.85) is the hard lower bound for F. F itself (absorption times first-pass survival) was not measured; metabolism is minimal.
